title: Unauthorized physical access (tailgating, piggybacking, lock bypass)
goal_html: Students analyze a printed building access log, identify records that indicate tailgating or impossible-speed violations, and propose one countermeasure for each flagged event. Ties to LO 2.2.A (identify indicators of unauthorized physical access) and 2.2.B (explain how physical attacks bypass access controls).
reference_html:
Printed log (use if machines unavailable)

steps_html:
1. (10 min) Each pair reviews the log table (or uses the simulation). For each event, decide: legitimate, suspicious, or impossible. Write "L", "S", or "I" next to the event ID and a one-sentence reason.
  2. (8 min) For every suspicious or impossible event, write the name of the attack technique it most likely represents (tailgating, piggybacking, RFID cloning, lock bypass, etc.) and one specific countermeasure the organization could deploy.
  3. (7 min) Pairs compare findings with the pair next to them. Resolve any disagreements: if you classified the same event differently, which argument is stronger?
collaborate_html: Assign roles: one partner is the "security analyst" (flags records and names the attack), the other is the "CISO" (approves or challenges each flag and selects the countermeasure). Swap roles halfway through the log.
exit_html: Each student submits: the event ID they found most ambiguous, the attack technique it represents, and the countermeasure they would implement, in two sentences or fewer.
